title: Console fabric grid and rollout inspector guidelines
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Define a cohesive ‘fabric’ (layout grid, elevation, spacing scale) and a set of reusable components and interaction patterns for the Rollout Inspector and adjacent cost dashboards. This ticket consolidates earlier prototypes into a single Figma library, prescribes responsive behavior, accessibility constraints, visual density options, and handoff tokens for engineering.

Scope:
- Establish a 4-step fabric: base grid (8px system with 12-column responsive breakpoints), surface elevations (3 levels with contrast guidelines), spacing scale, and micro-motion rules.
- Create a Rollout Inspector component family: rollout header, status timeline, canary control, traffic-split slider, fallback card, and audit timeline.
- Cost rail components: condensed metric chips, trend sparkline primitives, tokenized currency formatting components.
- Figma library: components, variants, and variable token page with usage examples and copy guidelines.
- Accessibility: keyboard-first interactions for timeline scrubber, color contrast checks for state badges, aria-label recommendations.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We keep 8px base spacing to remain consistent with console-wide components, even though tighter density (6px) would save screen real estate for metric-heavy pages — decision favors consistency for discoverability.
- Elevation palette is intentionally subtle to avoid visual noise in dashboards where scans must find anomalies quickly.
- The rollout slider will be native HTML range in the first release for reliability; we will migrate to a custom canvas-based control if usability studies indicate need.

Deliverables:
- Figma library file with components and tokens (dev-ready).
- Specification doc with interaction states and accessibility checklist.
- Implementation handoff packet (tokens.json, example CSS vars, React prop contract examples).

Success metrics:
- Engineering reports <2 design clarifications during first implementation sprint.
- Usability test NPS for rollout tasks >= 70.
- Visual QA pass rate >= 95% against tokenized spec.
